content.rationale:
The dependent is the flat module `src/verb_drafts.rs` (szmuyqrq), and the prerequisites its use leans on are artifacts: the route table's handler shape and the verb name (ynvwvzrm, nzrnrlky), the resolved context (zttrwlts), the refusal value (popowxnw), the lines-not-streams output contract (utrzvyyt), the argument surface and per-verb help (qtqnuqxo, xlvoxmyl, rwlywqrk), the registry module with its read refusal (rroqqrzq, ntypuupx), the workspace module (tyoypkmp) and the jj seam it crosses with. Both sides are code, so this edge is code-to-code and the check is a test: a self-contained crate per M-tests (knqkxzns), `tests/verb_drafts/`, which pulls the module under test and the siblings it calls in through `#[path]` shims and drives `verb_drafts::run(&Context, &[String]) -> Result<Vec<String>, Refusal>` over scratch jj repositories (`jj git init`) and a scratch draft-workspace root outside them. The compile-time `Verb<Context>` row named `drafts` ties the handler to the route table and to the one lowercase verb the decision settles. The crate uses serde_json for fixtures and, because the included registry module compiles its embedded schema with `jsonschema`, the validator the registry's own gate fixes; nothing here touches the round's repositories, nodes or changes.

The listing use is checked through the observables nzrnrlky and qspsyqlp fix. Records are written at `.deccy/work/<handle>.json`; a bare call is made; and the crate asserts one line per record and nothing outside the scan, each line naming its handle, its state and the workspace the record carries by name and path. Two records naming one node are kept as two rows, because the handle is the record's key and a node is only a reference. A record state is the landing fact (vkkwusty), so the line must carry `open` or `landed` as the record carries it.

The drift use is vuopwuyo and yozqornv applied to the listing. jj owns whether a workspace exists, the registry owns what the record means, and only an open record asserts a draft being written in its workspace. The crate takes an open record and a landed record whose named workspaces are absent, then creates both workspaces with real jj at the paths the records carry and lists again. The open record's line must carry the drift report exactly when the workspace is absent and must not carry it when the workspace is present — the report is read off those two cases as the word one has and the other lacks, so no wording is fixed — while the landed record's line must carry no drift in either case, because a landed record whose workspace is gone is the normal end of the draft and not drift. Forgetting the open record's workspace must make it as absent as one never created. The crate never asks how the verb matches a name and a path to one of jj's workspaces, which nzrnrlky leaves open; it makes the two agree so either reading sees the workspace.

The read-only use is yozqornv and vuopwuyo checked as effects, not wording. Around a listing, the exact bytes of every file under `.deccy/work` and the names under `nodes/` must be unchanged, the drifted record must still be `open` and still name its workspace, and the missing workspace must not have been created: the report is the whole effect, and a repair would destroy the difference it reports. The same no-write stance is asserted around the argument refusal.

The surface use is qtqnuqxo and xlvoxmyl. The verb declares no arguments in v1, so every argument count is refused naming a supplied argument — the crate exercises one argument and two — and neither refusal reads or writes the registry; the crate makes the ordering observable with a root-less context, where a workspace read would refuse for the absent root without evidence, so a refusal that names the argument can only come from the surface answering before the workspace is read. `--help` must answer from the same root-less context with a non-empty line naming the verb it describes. rwlywqrk's shared human-readable conventions are not asserted beyond that line, and the exact help wording is left open.

The registry and workspace modules do not exist at the revision this gate is authored against, so the shims fail to resolve and the red names the missing paths; that is an interface red naming the modules the candidate supplies, and the same command turns green when `src/verb_drafts.rs` and the sibling modules it calls are present and the observables above hold. Nothing here fixes the output's exact wording beyond the references the report must name, the exit status, the jj invocation, or how a record's workspace name and path are matched; those are open in nzrnrlky and are not demanded. The registry's own validation (ntypuupx) is not restated: a malformed record is refused by the registry module and checked by its own gate, and the verb is not asked for a behaviour the decision does not state.

The linked-workspace use is mrwtusss. mrwtusss confines the refusal of a non-trunk invocation to graph-writing verbs; the drafts verb writes nothing (vuopwuyo, yozqornv), so it must answer from a linked workspace instead of refusing there. Because the repository has one registry — the records under the trunk's `.deccy/work/` — the listing from a linked workspace is those records, not whatever the linked workspace's own tree holds. The crate makes a scratch repository, adds a second workspace with real `jj workspace add`, files a conforming record in the trunk's registry, and makes a bare call from the linked workspace: the call answers rather than refusing, the listing is not empty, and its line names the trunk record's handle, state and workspace by name and path. A second, differently handled record written into the linked workspace's own `.deccy/work/` after that call changes nothing in the listing, so the invocation tree is not read as a second registry.\n\nThe linked-workspace use also holds when the trunk has no registry at all. The case `a_linked_workspace_with_no_trunk_registry_lists_nothing` makes a scratch repository, adds a linked workspace with real `jj workspace add`, removes the trunk's `.deccy/work/`, files one conforming record only in the linked workspace's own `.deccy/work/`, and makes a bare call from the linked workspace. Its pass condition is an empty listing, twice over: with the trunk registry directory absent, where the scan returns no records, and with a trunk registry directory recreated but empty, where it still returns none; the linked record's handle appears in neither listing. This holds the listing to `.deccy/work` under the store root and never the invocation workspace's own tree, and it is aimed at the fallback the earlier case could not see: because that case always filed a trunk record before listing, a verb that scanned the store root but fell back to the invocation workspace's `.deccy/work/` whenever the trunk registry directory was absent listed the trunk record and satisfied it while reading the wrong tree. With the trunk registry absent, that fallback lists the linked record, and only a scan rooted at the store root in every case yields the empty listing the case requires.
